# How we work with AI on FPV Drone

<!-- Generated by ai-native-blueprint v0.1.1. One page, team-owned. -->

## The loop

`/triage <issue>` → refine until agent-executable → `/workon <issue>` → implementation PR →
`/review <pr>` → human merges.

Skills live in `.claude/skills/`: `triage`, `workon`, `review`, `write-tests`, `parallel-work`,
`doctor`, `init`. They are copies — rewrite them to fit how this project actually works.

## Who does what

- **Humans own**: intent, architecture, acceptance, merging. The PR author is accountable for
  the change regardless of who typed it.
- **Agents own**: first drafts, tests, routine changes, review findings.

Two rules specific to this project, both from `CLAUDE.md`:

- The Hytale API is undocumented — an agent must read the decompiled sources before writing
  anything touching `com.hypixel.*`. Guessed API calls are the main failure mode here.
- Physics, curves, crossings and race state land with a unit test. Flying around is not
  verification.

## Boundaries

See `CLAUDE.md` → Boundaries for the always/ask-first/never lists, and `.claude/settings.json`
for the machine-enforced subset. No client constraints — personal project, no third-party data.

## Tools & auth

GitHub Issues and PRs via `gh` (keyring auth, account `maartenpeels2`); git over SSH. No
tracker beyond GitHub Issues.

## Keeping this healthy

Run `doctor` when agents start failing at tasks they used to handle. Fix broken commands in
`CLAUDE.md` the moment you notice them.

Known gap, deliberate: **no commit-time hooks.** There is no secret scan or protected-path
hook, because this repo has no hook mechanism and adding one wasn't worth it for a solo
project. `.claude/settings.json` guards the agent; nothing guards a manual `git commit`. If
that changes, `.claude/skills/init/SKILL.md` describes the two options.
